Let $G$ be a group and $b \in G$. Let $H$ be a subgroup of $G$. Define the set

$$
H_b=\{bab^{-1}: a\in H\}.
$$

Prove that $H_b$ is a subgroup of $G$.

questions.markdown: How many permutations of $n$ distinct elements $1,2,\ldots,n$ are there in which the element $k$ is not in the $k^{\text{th}}$ position for any $k$? $(1 \leq k \leq n)$

A partition of an integer $n$ is called self-conjugate if the Ferrers diagram of the partition is equal to its own transpose. Using Ferrers diagram, show that the number of self-conjugate partitions of $n$ equals the number of partitions of $n$ into distinct odd parts.
Show that for any $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$ in a lattice $(A, \leq)$ if $a \leq b$ and $c \leq d$, then $a \vee c \leq b \vee d$ and $a \wedge c \leq b \wedge d$.

Let

$$
E(x_1,x_2,x_3)=\overline{x_1} \vee \overline{\left(\overline{x_2} \vee (\overline{x_3} \wedge x_1)\right)}
$$

be a Boolean expression over the two-valued Boolean algebra $({\{0,1\}}, \vee, \wedge, \overline{\phantom{x}})$. Write $E(x_1,x_2,x_3)$ in both disjunctive and conjunctive normal forms.
Find both the 73rd and 115th permutations of $0$, $1$, $2$, $3$, $4$ in each of (i) reverse lexicographical order and (ii) Fike's order.
Show that $R$ is a valid inference from the premises $P$, $P \to Q$, $Q \to R$.

Demonstrate that $\; (\forall x)(S(x) \to Q(x))\;$ is a valid inference from the premises

$$
(\forall x)(P(x) \to Q(x)),
$$

$$
(\forall x)(\neg P(x) \to R(x)),
$$

$$
(\forall x)(R(x) \to \neg S(x)).
$$

Let $(A, \vee, \wedge, \overline{\phantom{x}})$ be a finite Boolean algebra. Let $b$ be any non-zero element in $A$, and $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_k$ be all the atoms of $A$ such that $a_i \leq b, i=1, 2, \ldots, k$. Then show that $b$ can be represented as the join of these atoms as

$$
b=a_1 \vee a_2 \vee \cdots \vee a_k.
$$
